stances.claim: Bar exam topnotcher Sean James Borja's openly gay identity, combined with his Ateneo class-topping, moot-court victories here and abroad, and bar exam first-place finish, debunks the myth 'that members of the LGBT are meant only for entertainment' and demonstrates the futility of judging a person 'not good enough' simply because they are 'different.'

FLP's selection process -- applying the same two requirements (academic excellence + leadership; ability to internalize liberty-prosperity-rule-of-law philosophy) without 'discrimination as to gender, race, color, religious belief, economic status or political affiliation' -- has been 'proven right' as a meritocratic talent-identification mechanism, with Borja's outcomes as evidence.
stances.confidence: asserted with first-person institutional voice ('we were proven right')

stances.claim: FLP's scholarship infrastructure -- funded by the Tan Yan Kee Foundation at P200,000 per scholar per year since 2016 -- produces results: every member of the first graduating batch passed the 2019 bar, including Borja (1st), Gaw (5th), and Dy (17th); FLP recognizes top performers with additional cash awards (P200,000 bar topnotcher, P100,000 fifth-placer, P25,000 class topper).
stances.confidence: asserted with named-scholar evidence and prize amounts

stances.claim: Beyond the scholarship program, FLP sponsors the Ayala Corp.-funded Dissertation Writing Contest with substantial prize money (P300,000 first / P200,000 second / P100,000 third / P20,000 finalist) and a board of judges including SC justices, retired SC justices, the PALS president, and the Ayala general counsel -- modeling philanthropic seriousness in legal scholarship.
stances.confidence: asserted with named judges and amounts

notable_anecdotes: Borja's own quoted self-description -- debunking 'the myth that members of the LGBT (lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender) are meant only for entertainment' -- placed at the top of the column to set the stake.

Borja's recounted history of being 'bullied, discriminated against and deprived of opportunities just because he was thought to be not good enough, just because he was different' -- providing the lived background against which his bar topping reads as institutional vindication.

FLP's institutional voice -- 'we did not treat him differently... we gave him the same opportunity without any discrimination as to gender, race, color, religious belief, economic status or political affiliation' -- a public statement of selection-process neutrality CJ ratifies first-person.

The full prize-money architecture made transparent: P200,000/scholar/year base funding from TYKF; P200,000 bar-topping bonus; P100,000 5th-place bonus; P25,000 class-topper or cum-laude bonus -- institutional rigor expressed in numbers.

The closing four-adjective benediction: 'excellent, diligent, dignified and gay, and we're mighty proud of him!' -- the integration of 'gay' into a string of merit-adjectives is the column's rhetorical achievement.

The fully-named board memberships -- scholarship judges chaired by Justice Antonio T. Carpio with TYKF executive Elizabeth T. Alba and Prof. Tanya Karina A. Lat; dissertation judges chaired by Justice Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe with Ayala GC Solomon M. Hermosura -- modeling the kind of public institutional transparency FLP advocates.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban celebrates 2019 bar exam top scorer Sean James Borja of Ateneo de Manila University, who 'frankly admitted he is gay' while debunking 'the myth that members of the LGBT are meant only for entertainment.' Despite having been 'bullied, discriminated against and deprived of opportunities just because he was thought to be not good enough, just because he was different,' Borja was selected -- along with 20 others -- when the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity's scholarship program launched in 2016, funded by the Tan Yan Kee Foundation at P200,000 per scholar per year. FLP, CJ writes in the institutional first person, 'did not treat him differently' but applied the same two requirements as for all applicants: academic excellence plus leadership, and the ability and willingness to internalize and espouse the philosophy of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law -- 'without any discrimination as to gender, race, color, religious belief, economic status or political affiliation.' Borja topped his class at Ateneo, won moot courts here and abroad, and now aces the bar, earning an additional P200,000 for topping the SC tests and P25,000 for being Ateneo valedictorian. Every member of the first graduating batch (2018) passed the 2019 bar, including Katrina Monica Gaw (AdMU, 5th place, P100,000), Karina Mae Badua, Ervin Fredrick Dy (UP, 17th), Rexlyn Anne Evora (PUP), Summerson Macasarte (St. Thomas More), Nigel Carmelo Reago (La Salle), Jose Angelo Tiglao (La Salle), Althea Vergara (USC), and Vanessa Gloria Vergara (AdMU); class toppers Evora, Reago, Macasarte, and former scholar Jose Noel Hilario (UST, cum laude) each receive P25,000. CJ rosters the ten current fourth-year and ten current third-year scholars by name and university, names the scholarship board of judges chaired by Justice Antonio T. Carpio, and reports the Ayala Corp.-funded Dissertation Writing Contest winners -- Josiah David Quising (FEU, P300,000 first), Diana Lou Boado (Lyceum, P200,000 second), three third-place finishers at P100,000 each (De Belen of San Beda, Lumbera of Lumsa Rome, Sawali of FEU), and five finalists at P20,000 each -- with a dissertation board chaired by Justice Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe. All recipients will be honored at the FLP convocation at AdMU's Rockwell auditorium at 5 p.m. on May 18, 2019. CJ closes with the line that integrates protected-class identity into a merit benediction: Borja is 'excellent, diligent, dignified and gay, and we're mighty proud of him!'
